historical_claims.anchor: Jacques Dixmier studied the relative position of two closed subspaces of a Hilbert space in 1948, and Chandler Davis's 1958 paper on the separation of two linear subspaces placed the cosine and sine data in an operator-theoretic setting through closeness and separation operators.
historical_claims.source_locator: Böttcher and Spitkovsky (2010), Remark 1.3, for Dixmier (1948); Davis (1958), closeness and separation operators; journal paper Section 2.3

historical_claims.anchor: In their 1970 paper, Davis and Kahan define Theta as an operator from the start, precisely because the spectral subspaces they study need not be finite-dimensional.
